dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3101.text: The base of bells and drums, decorated as a fierce beast: from 虍, with 異 depicting its feet below.

shuowen:3102.text: Lord of the mountain beasts. From 虍; a tiger's feet resemble human feet. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 虎.

shuowen:3103.text: A tiger's sound. From 虎; 毄 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 隔.

shuowen:3104.text: A white tiger. From 虎; abbreviated 昔 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 鼏.

shuowen:3105.text: A kind of white tiger, 䖑. From 虎; 去 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3106.text: A black tiger. From 虎; 儵 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3107.text: A tiger with pale-colored fur is called 虦苗. From 虎; 戔 supplies the sound. 竊 means light or shallow.

shuowen:3108.text: Tiger markings. From 虎; 彡 depicts the markings.

shuowen:3109.text: The appearance of a tiger. From 虎; 乂 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3110.text: The appearance of a tiger. From 虎; 气 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3111.text: A tiger's roar. Another explanation: a lion. From 虎; 九 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3112.text: A tiger's sound. From 虎; 斤 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3113.text: The Changes says: “Treading on a tiger's tail, fearful.” Fear. Another explanation: a fly-tiger spider. From 虎; 𡭴 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3114.text: Clear marks scratched by a tiger. From 虎; 寽 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3115.text: 委虒, a tiger with horns. From 虎; 𠂆 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3116.text: A black tiger. From 虎; 騰 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3117.text: Cruel; urgent. From 虎 and 武. It appears in the Rites of Zhou.

shuowen:3118.text: People of Chu call a tiger 烏䖘. From 虎; 兔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3119.text: A tiger's anger. From two 虎. All graphs in this category contain 虤.

shuowen:3120.text: The sound of two tigers fighting. From 虤 and 曰. Pronounced like 憖.

shuowen:3121.text: To divide or distinguish. From 虤 facing each other and contending over 貝. Pronounced like 迴.

shuowen:3122.text: A vessel for food. A pictograph, sharing the idea of 豆. All graphs in this category contain 皿. Pronounced like 猛.

shuowen:3123.text: A food vessel. From 皿; 亏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3124.text: A small bowl. From 皿; 夗 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3125.text: Millet in a vessel for sacrifice. From 皿; 成 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3126.text: Millet in a vessel for sacrifice. From 皿; 齊 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3127.text: A small bowl. From 皿; 有 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 灰; another pronunciation is like 賄.

shuowen:3128.text: A food vessel. From 皿; 𧇄 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3129.text: A vessel. From 皿 and 缶; 古 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3130.text: A vessel. From 皿; 弔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3131.text: A basin. From 皿; 央 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3132.text: A basin. From 皿; 分 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3133.text: A vessel. From 皿; 宁 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3134.text: 㯯盨, a vessel carried on the back or head. From 皿; 須 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3135.text: A vessel. From 皿; 漻 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3136.text: An implement or vessel. From 皿; 必 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3137.text: Sour. Vinegar is made using 𩱙 and wine. From abbreviated 𩱙 and 酒, and from 皿; 皿 is a vessel. [The ingredient 𩱙 is not further explained.]

shuowen:3138.text: To blend flavors. From 皿; 禾 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3139.text: Abundance. From 水 and 皿; 皿 conveys increase.

shuowen:3140.text: A vessel full. From 皿 and 夃.

shuowen:3141.text: A vessel empty within. From 皿; 㶳 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3142.text: A vessel empty. From 皿; 中 supplies the sound. The Laozi says: “The Way is empty, yet one uses it.”

shuowen:3143.text: To cover. From 皿; 酓 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3144.text: Benevolence. From 皿, using it to feed a prisoner. Guan Pu's explanation.

shuowen:3145.text: To wash the hands. From 𦥑, with 水 over 皿. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Presenting the basin, pour water for washing.”

shuowen:3146.text: To wash vessels. From 皿; 湯 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3147.text: The 盋 vessel, a kind of bowl. From 皿; 犮 supplies the sound. Alternatively from 金 and 本.

shuowen:3148.text: 𠙴盧, a food vessel made of willow. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 𠙴.

shuowen:3149.text: People separating from one another. From 大; 凵 supplies the sound. All graphs in this category contain 去.

shuowen:3150.text: To go away. From 去; 曷 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3151.text: To go away. From 去; 夌 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 陵.

shuowen:3152.text: The blood of a sacrificial victim presented in sacrifice. From 皿; 一 depicts blood. All graphs in this category contain 血.

shuowen:3153.text: Blood. From 血; 亡 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The man stabbed the sheep, yet there was no blood.”

shuowen:3154.text: Congealed blood. From 血; 不 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3155.text: Vital fluid. From 血; 𦘔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3156.text: To settle one's breathing. From 血; abbreviated 甹 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 亭.

shuowen:3157.text: Blood issuing from the nose. From 血; 丑 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3158.text: Swollen or pooled blood. From 血; abbreviated 䢉 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3159.text: Blood sauce. From 血; 䏙 supplies the sound. The Record of Rites has 𧖺醢, made with dried beef, fine grain, 𥶶, salt and wine.

shuowen:3160.text: Meat sauce. From 血; 菹 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3161.text: A sacrifice in which blood is cut out and smeared on something. From 血; 幾 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3162.text: To worry. From 血; 卩 supplies the sound. Another explanation: scarce or few.

shuowen:3163.text: Grief and pain. From 血 and 聿; 皕 supplies the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “None of the people fail to feel grief that wounds the heart.”

shuowen:3164.text: Congealed sheep's blood. From 血; 臽 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3165.text: To cover. From 血 and 大.

shuowen:3166.text: Defiled blood. From 血; 蔑 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3167.text: Where something ends or stops, a dot marks it. All graphs in this category contain 丶.

shuowen:3168.text: The flame-core in a lamp. From 纹, pictographic, and from 丶, which also supplies the sound. [The unusual recorded component 纹 is preserved.]

shuowen:3169.text: When speaking to one another, to spit and refuse acceptance. From 丶 and 否; 否 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:3170.text: A red stone from Ba and Yue. It depicts a cinnabar-mining well; 一 depicts the cinnabar. All graphs in this category contain 丹.

shuowen:3171.text: Good cinnabar pigment. From 丹; 蒦 supplies the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Only the preparation of red pigment.” Pronounced like 隺.

shuowen:3172.text: Decoration in cinnabar. From 丹 and 彡; 彡 is its painting.

shuowen:3173.text: The color of the east. Wood produces fire, hence from 生 and 丹. The steadfastness of cinnabar and blue-green is expressed by this form. All graphs in this category contain 青. [The phrase 丹青之信言象然 is uncertain.]

shuowen:3174.text: Careful examination. From 青; 爭 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3175.text: Eight households share one well. It depicts the constructed well-curb; • depicts the bucket 𦉥. Anciently Boyi first made wells. All graphs in this category contain 井.

shuowen:3176.text: A deep pool. From 井; abbreviated 瑩 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3177.text: A pitfall. From 𨸏 and 井; 井 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:3178.text: To punish offenses. From 井 and 刀. The Changes says: “井 means law.” 井 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:3179.text: To establish laws and begin undertakings. From 井; 刅 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 創.

shuowen:3180.text: The fragrance of grain. It depicts fine grain within a wrapping; 匕 is used to scoop it. Another account: 皀 is one grain. All graphs in this category contain 皀. Also pronounced like 香.

shuowen:3181.text: To approach food. From 皀; 卪 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3182.text: To eat a little. From 皀; 旡 supplies the sound. The Analects says: “He did not allow it to exceed the staple food.” [The quoted wording is difficult.]

shuowen:3183.text: Rice unevenly hard and soft, sticking together. From 皀; 冂 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 適.

shuowen:3184.text: Black millet brewed with 𩰪 herb: its fragrance spreads, bringing down spirits. From 凵, a vessel; the middle depicts rice, and 匕 scoops it. The Changes says: “Not losing the ladle and fragrant wine.” All graphs in this category contain 鬯.

shuowen:3185.text: A fragrant herb. Ten leaves make one string; a hundred and twenty strings are pounded and boiled to make 𩰪. From 𦥑, 冂, 缶 and 鬯; 彡 is its ornament. Another explanation: 𩰪鬯 is the essence of the hundred herbs; fragrant herbs sent as tribute by the distant 𩰪 people are brewed together to bring down spirits. 𩰪 is now Yulin commandery.

shuowen:3186.text: A ritual vessel. It depicts the vessel, containing fragrant wine and held by 又, for drinking. Its bird-like form is chosen because the bird calls rhythmically, 節節足足.

shuowen:3187.text: Black millet, two grains within one husk, used for brewing. From 鬯; 矩 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3188.text: To arrange in ranks. From 鬯; 吏 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 迅.

shuowen:3189.text: A portion of rice. From 皀; 亼 supplies the sound. Another account: 亼 and 皀 combined. All graphs in this category contain 食.

shuowen:3190.text: Soaked rice. From 食; 𠦪 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3191.text: Rice vapor steaming upward. From 食; 畱 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3192.text: Thoroughly cooked. From 食; 壬 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3193.text: Cooked food. From 食; 雝 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3194.text: Rice malt boiled down. From 食; 台 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3195.text: Malt syrup mixed with fried dough strands. From 食; 易 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3196.text: Roasted rice grain, 粻䅣. From 食; 𢿱 supplies the sound. [The food term is uncertain.]

shuowen:3197.text: A cake made from flour. From 食; 并 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3198.text: A rice cake. From 食; 次 supplies the sound.

shuowen:3199.text: Thick gruel. From 食; 亶 supplies the sound. Zhou calls it 饘; Song calls it 餬.

shuowen:3200.text: Dry provisions. From 食; 矦 supplies the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Store your dry provisions.”
